docs.title: Quantitative Statistics, CAPM & Regression Transforms (polars_anta.stats)
docs.text: The polars_anta.stats module provides 13 vectorized statistical, econometric, and stationarity primitives engineered for institutional factor standardization, systematic risk decomposition, rolling Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, and memory-preserving fractional differentiation.

docs.title: zscore(close, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation:

\[ Z_t = \frac{x_t - \hat{\mu}_t}{\hat{\sigma}_t}, \qquad \hat{\mu}_t = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_{t-i}, \qquad \hat{\sigma}_t = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n - 1}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^2} \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation: Measures how many rolling standard deviations the current observation lies away from its trailing mean. Widely used in statistical arbitrage (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion triggers when \(|Z_t| > 2.0\)) and time-series feature normalization.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Pure native Rust rolling_mean(period) and rolling_std(period) with zero-division protection (0.0 when \(\hat{\sigma}_t = 0\)).

docs.title: percentile_rank(close, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation:

\[ \text{PctRank}_t = \frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \left( \mathbb{I}_{\{x_{t-i} < x_t\}} + \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{I}_{\{x_{t-i} = x_t\}} \right) \in [0.0, 1.0] \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation: Non-parametric, outlier-resistant alternative to zscore. Because financial returns exhibit heavy tails where a single volatility shock can distort \(\hat{\sigma}_t\) for \(n\) subsequent bars, percentile_rank maps any fat-tailed distribution uniformly onto \([0, 1]\).
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Vectorized via zero-copy sliding_window_view pairwise comparison against the rightmost column windows[:, -1:].

docs.title: skewness(close, period=20) & kurtosis(close, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations:

\[ \hat{\gamma}_{3, t} = \frac{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^3}{\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^2\right)^{3/2}}, \qquad \hat{\gamma}_{4, t} = \frac{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^4}{\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_{t-i} - \hat{\mu}_t)^2\right)^{2}} - 3 \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation:
  • Skewness (\(\hat{\gamma}_3\)): Quantifies distributional asymmetry. Negative return skewness (\(\hat{\gamma}_3 < 0\)) warns of "crash risk" (frequent small gains punctuated by sharp drawdowns, typical of short-volatility or carry strategies).
  • Excess Kurtosis (\(\hat{\gamma}_4\)): Quantifies tail thickness relative to a Gaussian distribution (\(\gamma_4^{\text{normal}} = 0\)). High excess kurtosis signals regime instability and elevated probability of \(3\sigma+\) tail events.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Delegated directly to Polars' native streaming rolling_skew(period) and rolling_kurtosis(period) kernels in Rust.

docs.title: rolling_cov(x, y, period=20) & rolling_corr(x, y, period=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations:

\[ \text{Cov}_t(X, Y) = \frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (x_{t-i} - \bar{x}_t)(y_{t-i} - \bar{y}_t), \qquad \rho_t(X, Y) = \frac{\text{Cov}_t(X, Y)}{\hat{\sigma}_{X, t}\,\hat{\sigma}_{Y, t}} \in [-1, 1] \]
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Computed via Polars' native pl.rolling_cov(x, y, window_size=period) and pl.rolling_corr(x, y, window_size=period) in Rust.

docs.title: rolling_beta(asset_returns, benchmark_returns, period=60) & rolling_alpha(asset_returns, benchmark_returns, rf=0.0, period=60)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations (Sharpe-Lintner CAPM):

\[ \hat{\beta}_t = \frac{\text{Cov}_t(R_a, R_m)}{\text{Var}_t(R_m)}, \qquad \hat{\alpha}_t = (\bar{R}_{a, t} - r_f) - \hat{\beta}_t (\bar{R}_{m, t} - r_f) \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation:
  • rolling_beta measures time-varying systematic exposure of an asset or strategy \(R_a\) to the market benchmark \(R_m\) (e.g., VN30 Index). It is the foundational input for constructing Beta-Neutral long/short portfolios (\(w_i^{\text{hedged}} = w_i - \hat{\beta}_i w_m\)) and passing into orthogonalize.
  • rolling_alpha (Jensen's Alpha) isolates idiosyncratic return per period unexplained by systematic market drift.

docs.title: 3. Closed-Form Rolling OLS Linear Regression Suite
docs.text:
Fitting \(y_{t-n+1+i} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot i + \epsilon_i\) for \(i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}\) via exact WMA–SMA algebraic reduction (see Architecture & Mathematical Derivations):

Function Signature Closed-Form Identity Quantitative Use Case linear_regression_slope(close, period=14) \(\hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{6}{n - 1}\left(\text{WMA}_n - \text{SMA}_n\right)\) Velocity of price change per bar (\(112.4\times\) faster than rolling scipy.stats.linregress). linear_regression_intercept(close, period=14) \(\hat{\beta}_0 = 4\,\text{SMA}_n - 3\,\text{WMA}_n\) Fitted value at the start of the rolling window (\(i = 0\)). linear_regression_forecast(close, period=14) \(\hat{y}_t = \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1(n - 1) = 3\,\text{WMA}_n - 2\,\text{SMA}_n\) Zero-lag OLS end-of-window fair value estimate. linear_regression_angle(close, period=14) \(\theta_t = \arctan(\hat{\beta}_1) \cdot \frac{180}{\pi}\) Trend trajectory angle in degrees \((-90^\circ, +90^\circ)\).

docs.title: frac_diff(close, d=0.4, window=20)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (Fixed-Window Fractional Differentiation — López de Prado, 2018):

\[ \tilde{X}_t^{(d, W)} = \sum_{k=0}^{W-1} \omega_k X_{t-k}, \qquad \omega_0 = 1, \qquad \omega_k = -\omega_{k-1} \frac{d - k + 1}{k} \quad (k = 1, \dots, W - 1) \]
  • Quantitative Theory:
  • When \(d = 0.0\), \(\omega_0 = 1\) and \(\omega_k = 0\) (\(\forall k \ge 1\)), returning the raw non-stationary price series \(X_t\).
  • When \(d = 1.0\), \(\omega_0 = 1, \omega_1 = -1\), and \(\omega_k = 0\) (\(\forall k \ge 2\)), returning the standard first difference \(X_t - X_{t-1}\) (which is stationary but erases trend memory).
  • For fractional orders \(d \in (0, 1)\) (typically \(d \in [0.3, 0.5]\)), all weights \(\omega_k\) (\(k \ge 1\)) are negative and decay slowly according to a power law \(\omega_k \sim \frac{-d}{\Gamma(1-d)} k^{-d-1}\). This transformation removes unit-root non-stationarity so tree/neural ML models do not overfit to secular price levels, while preserving long-memory cointegration and support/resistance structure.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Precomputes the exact binomial weight vector w_rev = weights[::-1] once and executes a single BLAS matrix-vector product sliding_window_view(vals, window) @ w_rev inside map_batches, supporting multi-asset .over("symbol") partitioning.
import polars as pl
import polars_anta as pa

df = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("close").anta.frac_diff(d=0.4, window=20).over("symbol").alias("close_ffd_04")
)

docs.title: Trend Filters, Adaptive Moving Averages & Structural Pivots (polars_anta.trend)
docs.text: The polars_anta.trend module provides 28 low-lag moving averages, adaptive digital filters, directional regime classifiers, volatility trailing stops, and structural pivot levels.

docs.title: 1. Linear, Low-Lag & Gaussian Moving Averages
docs.text:
In digital signal processing (DSP), a moving average is a low-pass filter that attenuates high-frequency market noise at the cost of phase lag. polars-anta provides a full hierarchy of linear and zero-lag filters:

Function Signature Mathematical Definition Phase Lag & Filter Characteristics sma(close, period=10) \(\text{SMA}_t(n) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} C_{t-i}\) Equal weights; group delay of \(\frac{n - 1}{2}\) bars. ema(close, period=10) \(\text{EMA}_t(n) = \alpha C_t + (1 - \alpha)\text{EMA}_{t-1}(n), \quad \alpha = \frac{2}{n + 1}\) Infinite impulse response (IIR) filter; center-of-mass lag of \(\frac{n - 1}{2}\) bars with higher recent weight. wma(close, period=10) \(\text{WMA}_t(n) = \frac{2}{n(n + 1)} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (n - i) C_{t-i}\) Triangular weight profile; reduces group delay to \(\frac{n - 1}{3}\) bars. hma(close, period=10) \(\text{HMA}_t(n) = \text{WMA}_{\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor}\!\left(2\,\text{WMA}_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}(C_t) - \text{WMA}_n(C_t)\right)\) Alan Hull's algebraic lag cancellation; eliminates first-order linear phase lag while maintaining smoothness. dema(close, period=10) \(\text{DEMA}_t = 2 E_1 - E_2\), where \(E_1 = \text{EMA}_n(C), E_2 = \text{EMA}_n(E_1)\) Patrick Mulloy's second-order error-correcting exponential filter. tema(close, period=10) \(\text{TEMA}_t = 3 E_1 - 3 E_2 + E_3\), where \(E_3 = \text{EMA}_n(E_2)\) Third-order error cancellation for steep trend tracking. zlema(close, period=10) \(\text{ZLEMA}_t = \text{EMA}_n\!\left(C_t + (C_t - C_{t - \lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor})\right)\) Pre-compensates input price by adding the momentum over the filter's half-window lag. t3(close, period=5, vfactor=0.7) \(\text{T3}_t = c_1 E_6 + c_2 E_5 + c_3 E_4 + c_4 E_3\) (\(6\)-stage cascaded EMA) Tim Tillson's generalized DEMA cascade; combines low phase lag with minimal overshoot. alma(close, period=9, offset=0.85, sigma=6.0) \(\text{ALMA}_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i C_{t-n+1+i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i}, \quad w_i = \exp\!\left(-\frac{(i - m)^2}{2 s^2}\right)\) Arnaud Legoux's shifted Gaussian bell-curve convolution (\(m = \text{offset}(n-1), s = n/\sigma\)).

docs.title: 2. Non-Linear Adaptive Moving Averages
docs.text: Unlike fixed-period filters, adaptive moving averages dynamically modulate their smoothing constant \(\alpha_t\) based on market efficiency or momentum:

docs.title: kama(close, period=10, fast_period=2, slow_period=30)
docs.text:
Perry Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average: Computes the Efficiency Ratio (\(\text{ER}_t \in [0, 1]\)) — the ratio of net directional displacement to total path length:

\[ \text{ER}_t = \frac{|C_t - C_{t-n}|}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} |C_{t-i} - C_{t-i-1}|}, \qquad \text{SC}_t = \left[ \text{ER}_t (\alpha_{\text{fast}} - \alpha_{\text{slow}}) + \alpha_{\text{slow}} \right]^2 \] \[ \text{KAMA}_t = \text{KAMA}_{t-1} + \text{SC}_t (C_t - \text{KAMA}_{t-1}) \]

When price moves in a straight line (\(\text{ER}_t \to 1\)), \(\text{KAMA}_t\) tracks closely at fast_period; during sideways chop (\(\text{ER}_t \to 0\)), \(\text{SC}_t^2 \to \alpha_{\text{slow}}^2\), freezing the average flat to prevent whipsaws.

docs.title: vidya(close, period=14, hist_period=None) & mcginley_dynamic(close, period=14)
docs.text:
• Tushar Chande's VIDYA: Modulates \(\alpha_t = \alpha_0 \cdot |\text{CMO}_t| / 100\) using the absolute Chande Momentum Oscillator.
  • John McGinley's Dynamic Indicator: Adjusts smoothing inversely to the fourth power of price velocity:
\[ \text{MD}_t = \text{MD}_{t-1} + \frac{C_t - \text{MD}_{t-1}}{n \cdot (C_t / \text{MD}_{t-1})^4} \]

docs.title: 3. Directional Strength, Regime Classifiers & Trailing Stops
adx(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text:
J. Welles Wilder's Directional Movement System (pl.Struct: ("adx", "plus_di", "minus_di")):

\[ \text{+DM}_t = \max(H_t - H_{t-1}, 0)\,\mathbb{I}_{\{H_t - H_{t-1} > L_{t-1} - L_t\}}, \qquad \text{-DM}_t = \max(L_{t-1} - L_t, 0)\,\mathbb{I}_{\{L_{t-1} - L_t > H_t - H_{t-1}\}} \] \[ \text{+DI}_t = 100 \frac{\text{RMA}_n(\text{+DM}_t)}{\text{ATR}_t(n)}, \qquad \text{-DI}_t = 100 \frac{\text{RMA}_n(\text{-DM}_t)}{\text{ATR}_t(n)} \] \[ \text{DX}_t = 100 \frac{|\text{+DI}_t - \text{-DI}_t|}{\text{+DI}_t + \text{-DI}_t}, \qquad \text{ADX}_t = \text{RMA}_n(\text{DX}_t) \]

docs.title: chop(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text:
E.W. Dreiss's Choppiness Index (Fractal Consolidation Filter):

\[ \text{CHOP}_t(n) = 100 \cdot \frac{\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{TR}_{t-i}}{\max_{0 \le i < n} H_{t-i} - \min_{0 \le i < n} L_{t-i}}\right)}{\log_{10}(n)} \in [0, 100] \]
  • \(\text{CHOP}_t > 61.8\): Market is range-bound / consolidating (Fibonacci retracement threshold).
  • \(\text{CHOP}_t < 38.2\): Strong directional trend is underway.

docs.title: supertrend(high, low, close, period=10, multiplier=3.0) & psar(high, low, close=None, af_start=0.02, af_step=0.02, af_max=0.20)
docs.text:
• supertrend: Stateful ATR ratchet stop around \(\text{HL2}_t = (H_t + L_t)/2 \pm m \cdot \text{ATR}_t(n)\). Returns Struct(supertrend, direction) where direction is +1 (bullish) or -1 (bearish).
  • psar (Parabolic SAR): Wilder's accelerating stop-and-reverse parabola \(\text{SAR}_{t+1} = \text{SAR}_t + \text{AF}_t (\text{EP}_t - \text{SAR}_t)\) where the acceleration factor \(\text{AF}_t\) increments by af_step up to af_max whenever a new Extreme Point (\(\text{EP}_t\)) is reached.

docs.title: Volatility Estimators, ATR Stops & Price Channels (polars_anta.volatility)
docs.text: The polars_anta.volatility module provides 18 volatility estimators, range-based efficient variance models, and dynamic price channels used for position sizing, volatility targeting, breakout detection, and stop-loss placement.

docs.title: 1. High-Efficiency Range-Based Volatility Estimators
docs.text:
In continuous-time finance (\(d\ln P_t = \sigma\,dW_t\)), the standard Close-to-Close volatility estimator uses only two snapshots per bar (\(C_{t-1}\) and \(C_t\)), discarding all intraday path information (a stock that surges \(+5\%\) intraday and closes unchanged has zero close-to-close return).

polars-anta implements three classical annualized volatility estimators with increasing statistical asymptotic efficiency \(\text{Eff}(\hat{\sigma}^2) = \frac{\text{Var}(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{CC}}^2)}{\text{Var}(\hat{\sigma}^2)}\):

Estimator Function Signature Mathematical Formula (Annualized by \(\sqrt{A}\), default \(A = 252\)) Statistical Efficiency Close-to-Close historical_volatility(close, period=20, annualization=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{CC}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{n - 1}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left(r_{t-i} - \bar{r}_t\right)^2}, \quad r_t = \ln\frac{C_t}{C_{t-1}}\) \(1.0\times\) (Baseline) Parkinson (1980) parkinson_volatility(high, low, period=20, annualization=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{P}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{4 n \ln 2} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left(\ln\frac{H_{t-i}}{L_{t-i}}\right)^2}\) \(4.9\times\) Garman-Klass (1980) garman_klass_volatility(open, high, low, close, period=20, annualization=252) \(\hat{\sigma}_{\text{GK}, t} = \sqrt{A} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \left[\frac{1}{2}\left(\ln\frac{H_{t-i}}{L_{t-i}}\right)^2 - (2\ln 2 - 1)\left(\ln\frac{C_{t-i}}{O_{t-i}}\right)^2\right]}\) \(7.4\times\)

Quantitative Advantage of Garman-Klass

Because Garman-Klass achieves \(7.4\times\) higher statistical efficiency than Close-to-Close volatility, a 10-bar Garman-Klass estimator has lower estimation variance than a 70-bar Close-to-Close estimator, enabling much faster regime adaptation in Volatility Targeting (vol_target) and Triple-Barrier scaling without increasing estimation noise.

docs.title: 2. True Range, Wilder's ATR & Trailing Volatility Stops
true_range(high, low, close), atr(high, low, close, period=14), & natr(high, low, close, period=14)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulations (J. Welles Wilder Jr., 1978):

\[ \text{TR}_t = \max\left(H_t - L_t,\, |H_t - C_{t-1}|,\, |L_t - C_{t-1}|\right) \] \[ \text{ATR}_t(n) = \text{RMA}_n(\text{TR}_t) = \frac{(n - 1)\,\text{ATR}_{t-1} + \text{TR}_t}{n}, \qquad \text{NATR}_t(n) = \frac{\text{ATR}_t(n)}{C_t} \times 100 \]
  • Quantitative Interpretation: true_range accounts for overnight or inter-bar gaps (\(|H_t - C_{t-1}|\) and \(|L_t - C_{t-1}|\)). While atr is denominated in raw price points (ideal for sizing point stops on VN30F1M), natr normalizes by price level so volatility can be ranked cross-sectionally across assets trading at different nominal prices.
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Formulated as an exact ewm_mean(alpha=1.0 / period, adjust=False, min_samples=period) kernel in Rust.

docs.title: chandelier_exit(high, low, close, period=22, multiplier=3.0)
docs.text:
Chuck LeBeau's ATR Trailing Stop (pl.Struct: ("long_stop", "short_stop")):

\[ \text{LongStop}_t = \max_{0 \le i < n} H_{t-i} - m \cdot \text{ATR}_t(n), \qquad \text{ShortStop}_t = \min_{0 \le i < n} L_{t-i} + m \cdot \text{ATR}_t(n) \]

docs.title: ulcer_index(close, period=14)
docs.text:
Peter Martin's Downside Drawdown Volatility (1987): Unlike standard deviation (stddev), which penalizes upside rallies and downside crashes equally, ulcer_index measures the root-mean-square depth and duration of rolling percentage drawdowns:

\[ R_t = \frac{C_t - \max_{0 \le i < n} C_{t-i}}{\max_{0 \le i < n} C_{t-i}} \times 100 \le 0, \qquad \text{UI}_t(n) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} R_{t-i}^2} \]

docs.title: chaikin_volatility(high, low, ema_period=10, roc_period=10)
docs.text:
Measures the rate of expansion or contraction of the smoothed High-Low trading range:

\[ \text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t} = \text{EMA}_{n_1}(H_t - L_t), \qquad \text{ChaikinVol}_t = \frac{\text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t} - \text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t - n_2}}{\text{EMA}_{\text{HL}, t - n_2}} \times 100 \]

docs.title: Volume, Institutional VWAP & Money Flow (polars_anta.volume)
docs.text: The polars_anta.volume module provides 16 volume-weighted price benchmarks, institutional execution bands, and money-flow oscillators designed to track institutional accumulation/distribution and intraday fair value.

docs.title: vwap(high, low, close, volume, period=None)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation: Let Typical Price be \(\text{TP}_t = \frac{H_t + L_t + C_t}{3}\). - Cumulative Mode (period=None, default):

\[ \text{VWAP}_t = \frac{\sum_{\tau=1}^t \text{TP}_\tau \cdot V_\tau}{\sum_{\tau=1}^t V_\tau} \]
  • Rolling Window Mode (period=N):
\[ \text{VWAP}_t(N) = \frac{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \text{TP}_{t-k} \cdot V_{t-k}}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} V_{t-k}} \]

docs.title: vwap_bands(high, low, close, volume, period=None, mult1=1.0, mult2=2.0, mult3=3.0)
docs.text:
Mathematical Formulation (Volume-Weighted Standard Deviation Bands): Using the identity \(\text{Var}_V(\text{TP}) = \mathbb{E}_V[\text{TP}^2] - \left(\mathbb{E}_V[\text{TP}]\right)^2\):

\[ \sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t} = \sqrt{\max\left(0,\, \frac{\sum \text{TP}_\tau^2 \cdot V_\tau}{\sum V_\tau} - \text{VWAP}_t^2\right)} \] \[ \text{Upper}_{k, t} = \text{VWAP}_t + m_k \cdot \sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t}, \qquad \text{Lower}_{k, t} = \text{VWAP}_t - m_k \cdot \sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t} \quad (k \in \{1, 2, 3\}) \]

Returns a pl.Struct with fields ("vwap", "upper_1", "lower_1", "upper_2", "lower_2", "upper_3", "lower_3").

docs.title: session_vwap(high, low, close, volume, session_by=None, time_col="timestamp", mult1=1.0, mult2=2.0)
docs.text:
Session-Anchored Institutional VWAP with Deviation Z-Score: In intraday equity and index futures trading (such as VN30F1M), institutional execution algorithms benchmark fills against the Session VWAP that resets at the start of every trading day (pl.col(time_col).dt.date() when session_by=None, or custom session identifiers such as morning/afternoon sessions).

\[ \text{VWAP}_{t \in S} = \frac{\sum_{\tau \in S, \tau \le t} \text{TP}_\tau V_\tau}{\sum_{\tau \in S, \tau \le t} V_\tau}, \qquad Z_{\text{VWAP}, t} = \frac{\text{TP}_t - \text{VWAP}_{t \in S}}{\sigma_{\text{VWAP}, t \in S}} \]
  • Output pl.Struct Schema (prefix="session_" when unnest=True): ("vwap", "upper_1", "lower_1", "upper_2", "lower_2", "zscore").
  • Tech / Polars Execution: Uses native Polars .cum_sum().over(session_key) window partitioning, resetting cumulative sums across thousands of trading sessions in parallel with zero loops.

docs.title: vwma(close, volume, period=20)
docs.text:
Volume-Weighted Moving Average:

\[ \text{VWMA}_t(n) = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} C_{t-i} \cdot V_{t-i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} V_{t-i}} \]

Comparing \(\text{VWMA}_t(n) - \text{SMA}_t(n)\) reveals whether volume is concentrated on high-price bars (bullish institutional participation) or low-price bars.

docs.title: obv(close, volume) & pvt(close, volume)
docs.text:
• Joe Granville's On-Balance Volume (obv):
\[ \text{OBV}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \text{sign}(C_\tau - C_{\tau-1}) \cdot V_\tau \]
  • Price Volume Trend (pvt): Scales signed volume by proportional price return rather than a binary step function:
\[ \text{PVT}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \left(\frac{C_\tau - C_{\tau-1}}{C_{\tau-1}}\right) V_\tau \]

docs.title: adl(high, low, close, volume) & cmf(high, low, close, volume, period=20)
docs.text:
Both indicators rely on Marc Chaikin's Close Location Value (CLV), which locates the closing price within the bar's High-Low range \([-1, +1]\):

\[ \text{CLV}_t = \frac{(C_t - L_t) - (H_t - C_t)}{H_t - L_t} = \frac{2C_t - L_t - H_t}{H_t - L_t} \in [-1, +1] \]
  • Accumulation / Distribution Line (adl): \(\text{ADL}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \text{CLV}_\tau \cdot V_\tau\).
  • Chaikin Money Flow (cmf): \(n\)-period ratio of Money Flow Volume to total volume:
\[ \text{CMF}_t(n) = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{CLV}_{t-i} \cdot V_{t-i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} V_{t-i}} \in [-1, +1] \]

docs.title: mfi(high, low, close, volume, period=14)
docs.text:
Quong & Soudack's Money Flow Index (Volume-Weighted RSI): Let Raw Money Flow be \(\text{RMF}_t = \text{TP}_t \cdot V_t\). Partitioning \(\text{RMF}_t\) into positive flow (\(\text{TP}_t > \text{TP}_{t-1}\)) and negative flow (\(\text{TP}_t < \text{TP}_{t-1}\)) over window \(n\):

\[ \text{MFR}_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{RMF}_{t-i}^+}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \text{RMF}_{t-i}^-}, \qquad \text{MFI}_t = 100 - \frac{100}{1 + \text{MFR}_t} \in [0, 100] \]

docs.title: klinger(high, low, close, volume, fast_period=34, slow_period=55, signal_period=13)
docs.text:
Stephen Klinger's Volume Force Oscillator: Combines trend direction \(T_t = \text{sign}(\text{TP}_t - \text{TP}_{t-1})\), daily range \(dm_t = H_t - L_t\), and cumulative trend range \(cm_t\) into Volume Force \(\text{VF}_t = V_t \cdot \left|2\frac{dm_t}{cm_t} - 1\right| \cdot T_t \cdot 100\), then computes:

\[ \text{KVO}_t = \text{EMA}_{34}(\text{VF}_t) - \text{EMA}_{55}(\text{VF}_t), \qquad \text{Signal}_t = \text{EMA}_{13}(\text{KVO}_t) \]

Returns pl.Struct with fields ("klinger", "signal").

docs.title: eom, force_index, nvi, pvi, vpci, vr
docs.text: Function Signature Mathematical Definition Quantitative Interpretation eom(high, low, volume, period=14, scale=10000.0) \(\text{SMA}_n\left(\Delta\left(\frac{H_t + L_t}{2}\right) \cdot \frac{H_t - L_t}{V_t / \text{scale}}\right)\) Richard Arms' Ease of Movement: high positive values mean price advances on light volume (low overhead resistance). force_index(close, volume, period=13) \(\text{EMA}_n\left((C_t - C_{t-1}) \cdot V_t\right)\) Alexander Elder's Force Index combining direction, extent of price change, and volume. nvi(close, volume) / pvi(close, volume) Updates cumulative return index only on bars where \(V_t < V_{t-1}\) (nvi) or \(V_t > V_{t-1}\) (pvi) Norman Fosback's Smart-Money (nvi, active on quiet volume days) vs. Crowd-Activity (pvi) indices. vpci(close, volume, short_period=5, long_period=20) \(\text{VPC}_t \times \text{VPR}_t \times \text{VM}_t\) Buff Dormeier's Volume Price Confirmation Indicator measuring divergence between VWMA and SMA. vr(close, volume, period=26) \(\frac{\text{AV}_n + \frac{1}{2}\text{CV}_n}{\text{BV}_n + \frac{1}{2}\text{CV}_n} \times 100\) Up-Volume (\(\text{AV}_n\)) vs. Down-Volume (\(\text{BV}_n\)) Ratio.
